chunks: And through his chain of narration, from Ali (peace be upon him), he said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Ammar is upon the truth when he is killed between the two factions; one of the two factions is upon my way and my tradition, and the other is a deserter from the religion, exiting from it.'

key_terms.عَمَّارٌ: Ammar ibn Yasir, a prominent companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about Ammar's status when he is killed between two factions?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq, is a cornerstone of Shia eschatology, identifying the Battle of Siffin as the context where Ammar ibn Yasir, though killed by the side of Imam Ali (AS), is considered 'upon the truth' because his faction followed the Prophet's Sunnah. It establishes the theological principle that martyrdom in the correct faction validates one's standing, even if they err in judgment, distinguishing the Ahl al-Haqq from the Marqiqa (departed).

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-302 According to the same documentation, on the authority of Ali (a.s.)

the Prophet (S) said, “Once Ammar is killed, when he is caught between the two factions - one who abides by my way and traditions, while the other faction has departed from my religion - he is adhering to the right religion.”
